headline: Shifts Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for the increased electric generating capacity they demand, preventing these costs from being passed on to other customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Virginia voters, consumer advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger.
opponents: Data center industry, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers (potentially).
news_headline: Virginia Legislation Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to Users
news_summary: New legislation in Virginia shifts energy costs to high-demand users, requiring facilities using 25 MW or more to pay for increased generating capacity. This prevents these costs from being passed on to other customers and establishes voluntary demand flexibility programs.

headline: Requires Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water utilities providing water to data centers to report the total volume of water consumed, including reclaimed water, to state regulators.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental groups.
news_headline: Virginia Requires Data Center Water Use Reporting
news_summary: Virginia's SB 553 requires water utilities to report monthly volumes of potable and reclaimed water delivered to data centers. This legislation aims to provide state regulators with better information to make informed decisions about water resources, addressing concerns about dwindling groundwater.

headline: Establishes Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including sound profile examinations on nearby residential units and schools, and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Del. Joshua E. Thomas, community advocates, residents concerned about noise and environmental impacts.
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Siting Law Takes Effect
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, which took effect July 1, 2026, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments, including noise studies near homes and schools. While it mandates studies, the law does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving some discretion to local authorities.
